usageNotes: Stops a named system service on a specific cluster node; requires `Sys.Modify` on `/nodes/{node}`. Stopping critical services like `pvedaemon`, `pve-cluster`, `corosync`, or `sshd` will disrupt cluster communication, API access, or remote connectivity on that node — only use when the node can be recovered via console. The return value is a UPID string for the resulting task, which can be polled with the task status endpoint.

examples.summary: Stop the PVE firewall service on node pve1

destructiveReason: Immediately stops the target system service on the node, which can interrupt active connections, cluster coordination, or VM/container operations depending on which service is stopped.
tips: Stopping `corosync` or `pve-cluster` on a multi-node cluster will cause quorum loss or split-brain — coordinate with other nodes first.
Stopping `sshd` or `pveproxy` will cut off remote shell and web UI access; ensure console (IPMI/KVM) access is available before doing so.
Use the sibling `restart` endpoint instead of stop+start when you only need to reload a service config change.
The returned UPID can be tracked via GET /nodes/{node}/tasks/{upid}/status to confirm the service has fully stopped.
